title: Mega-Aggregate (Large-Cluster Aggregate)
damaged_code:
```rust
struct Product {
    id: ProductId,
    description: String,
    backlog_items: Vec<BacklogItem>, // Enclosed inside Product
    releases: Vec<Release>,           // Enclosed inside Product
    sprints: Vec<Sprint>,             // Enclosed inside Product
}
```
pattern: Designing a domain aggregate to encapsulate a massive tree of related entities that can be edited independently, treating them all as a single transactional unit.
why_bad: Causes extreme transactional lock contention. If user A updates a `Sprint` while user B adds a `BacklogItem`, they both lock the root `Product`, leading to database transaction aborts or rollbacks. It causes severe memory overhead because loading a single `Product` forces loading hundreds of unrelated backlog items, releases, and sprints.
detection: Identify aggregate roots that contain large collections (`Vec`, `HashMap`, `HashSet`) of other complex Entities (objects with their own lifetime and IDs).
counterexample: Cohesive parent-child relationships where the child cannot exist or be modified apart from the parent, and collections are naturally small (e.g., `Order` and `OrderLine`).
source: *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 10, "Aggregates" (Small Aggregate Design, p. 355 & Reference Other Aggregates by Identity, p. 359).
